text.p: SYDNEY, July 2 - Zinc prices charged higher once more during Tuesday LME trading, clocking up yet another 6-3/4 year high as technical tightness developed in the autumn months, traders said. Elsewhere on the base metals complex the trends were mixed, with copper and tin sagging, but aluminium, nickel and lead in the plus column.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.72 to 238.70.

On the LME zinc market, speculative buying was sucked in to a market that is tightening all the time. Cash/threes contracted into just $2/3 contango at one stage, with a hefty backwardation developing from the September date. Traders said the market continues to be underpinned by talk of major Far Eastern shorts battling against influential European merchants. Last trade was at $1,437, up $19.

Copper fluctuated throughout the session, as nervousness built up ahead of the crucial July traded option declarations on Wednesday. Last business was at $2,393, down $29 from Monday. Once the options and the uncertainties associated with delat-hedging are out of the way, the market has the potential to strike higher again, traders said.

Aluminium held onto the bridgehead above the $1,600 level, although there was plenty of overhead resistance and some producer-linked selling to prevent a significant advance. Prices finished at $1,603, up $5 from yesterday.
Nickel price movements were whippier during the afternoon, with the market scrapping its way to a higher close of $6,930, up $70.
The lead market gained from the strength of zinc, as well as some July/August borrowing, and prices climbed above $630. Three months ended at $636, up $9.
Tin, however, was depressed by quiet physicals and some softening in premiums, which resulted in some tired long liquidation. Three months ended at $5,530, down $40.
A quiet alloy market finished at a stable $1,450/55 a tonne.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower, pulled down by a collapse in the soy complex after a mild technical bounce earlier in the wheat pit, traders said. CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with July down 1-1/4 at $3.22-1/2 and September was down 3/4 at $3.31-1/2.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Tuesday, with gold testing news four-year lows, but platinum group metals (PGMs) ended little changed after seeing higher levels intraday. "The outlook for both gold and silver still looks bearish, though we saw a little consolidation today," FIMAT New York trader, John Tyree, said. COMEX August gold ended down 20 cents at $335.10 an ounce, though managed to hold above the life-of-contract low at $334.60 seen Monday. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was a moderately heavy 42,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $333.70/20 an ounce, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $333.70. At the London Tuesday morning fix gold saw a fresh four year low at $336.0 an ounce, compared to the New York close Monday at $333.70/20.

August Brent crude on the IPE closed almost one third of a dollar firmer in a technically strong market boosted by market expectations of bullish American Petroleum Institute (API) figures, good fund buying and strong fundamentals, brokers said. August Brent ended up 31 cents at $18.82 a barrel having followed NYMEX crude and products for most of the afternoon. NYMEX WTI August crude broke through the 40 day moving average on the back of expectations that tonight's figures from the API would show a decline in U.S. crude and gasoline stocks for the week ended June 27.
